title: Shared hand - Tripo reference
summary:
**Current candidate: v003, from a different angle and fresh AC6 references.** The owner rejected the earlier thumb and its unnatural bend. A new thumb-side view and strict side profile of the actual model now guide the image directly, preserving its open thumb position in front of the palm.

items.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Create ONE clean low-poly hand reference for the owner to use in Tripo, using these two screenshots of the SAME AC6 hand.

IMAGE 1 is the PRIMARY geometry, pose and camera reference: a thumb-side/palm three-quarter view, wrist on the LEFT and four fingers pointing RIGHT.
IMAGE 2 is the exact SIDE PROFILE of that hand, supplied to clarify the thumb. The four long fingers overlap in this side view; they are four, not one.

FIRST PRIORITY: faithfully preserve the actual thumb from these references. Copy its root location, offset IN FRONT OF the palm, short link lengths, joint orientation and relaxed OPEN pose. In image 1 the thumb is the short digit in the lower foreground, projecting from the heel of the palm toward the right. It is spatially opposed to the four fingers, not spread out across the palm's width. Image 2 shows the thumb and index finger in their common bending plane: a simple open diverging jaw profile. ALL thumb hinges turn on parallel axes matching the finger bending axes.
Do not invent a new thumb mechanism or change its pose. Do not twist the thumb, splay it sideways like a human thumb, fold it into a C-shaped hook, face its pad outward, create a perpendicular swivel or add an extra root pivot. Preserve the reference's simple gently angled thumb chain and clear gap between thumb and finger row. The thumbnail silhouette and mounting orientation are more important than decorative details.

Simplify this exact hand into low-poly geometry:
- Exactly FOUR separate long fingers plus the reference's ONE shorter opposing thumb.
- Four long fingers use plain three-link chamfered rectangular blocks and simple dark hinge barrels, with the same arrangement and slim proportions as the reference. Clear small gaps between all four fingers.
- Keep the reference's substantial palm-to-finger proportion. A large faceted center plate, two simple angular side rails and a dark structural recess. Remove small inset borders, bolts, repeated thin plates and fine mechanism detail.
- Keep a SHORT BROAD mechanical wrist attachment at the left end, approximately two-thirds of palm width: a simple faceted collar/drum with one stepped flange and a short thick mating face. Preserve the visible separation from palm. No thin long peg or Lego-style plug. Remove the FOREARM beyond this coupling, leaving only the complete hand and wrist connector.

CAMERA: preserve IMAGE 1's oblique thumb-side angle and horizontal orientation, wrist LEFT, fingers RIGHT, thumb in the LOWER FOREGROUND. Do not rotate it into a front-facing upright human-hand presentation. Ensure four individual long fingers, thumb and complete connector are visible. The palm and thumb's offset in depth must read clearly. Use image 2 only to resolve geometry, do not output a second view.
Presentation: isolated gray low-poly mechanical hand, matte light-gray armor and medium-dark gray joints, neutral soft studio light, pure white background. Entire object with generous white margins. One object, one landscape image, no arm, no Blender UI, no text, arrows, inset diagram, ghost pose, grid, weapon or stand.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Correct only the thumb hinges in the supplied image. Everything else stays exactly unchanged: four long fingers, the thumb's bent opposing C-shaped pose and tip location, larger palm, wrist coupling, camera, lighting and white background.

CRITICAL ERROR TO FIX: at the ROOT of the thumb, beside the lower-left palm, the dark barrel is currently VERTICAL, with a visible round TOP. That is an incorrect swivel. It must be a HORIZONTAL axle, oriented LEFT TO RIGHT across the palm, exactly parallel to the dark barrels at the bases of the four long fingers. The thumb's second hinge also must share that exact left-right axle orientation.

Replace the thumb ROOT connection with the SAME fork-and-barrel shape as a finger-base hinge: two fixed bracket ears on the LEFT and RIGHT of the root, a short horizontal dark cylinder between them, its circular end caps buried inside the left and right ears. We should see the CURVED SIDE of the horizontal cylinder from this camera, like the finger knuckles. There must be NO visible circular TOP surface, NO vertical-axis drum, NO rotating platform, NO front-facing circular bolt, and NO second perpendicular joint.
Replace the smaller thumb inter-link hinge with the same horizontal finger-style barrel and left-right bracket ears. Its rotation axis is parallel to the root's and to all FOUR finger hinge barrels.
The thumb is therefore fixed to bend only front-to-back along the fingers' grip direction, as an OPPOSING JAW. Keep the bent hook pose of the thumb, with its pad facing toward the four fingers. Do not straighten the thumb or splay it sideways.

This is a small surgical correction of two hinge joints, not a hand redesign. Preserve all other pixels and forms as closely as possible. No labels or arrows.

items.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit the supplied mechanical hand image. CHANGE ONLY THE THUMB'S POSITION AND BEND. Preserve the four long fingers, enlarged armored palm, wrist coupling, white background, material, camera and framing exactly.

The thumb currently looks like a fifth finger: upright, coplanar and facing the same way as the four fingers. It must instead be a TRUE OPPOSING JAW.
Keep the thumb root on the lower thumb-side palm. Keep ALL its hinge axles exactly PARALLEL TO THE FOUR FINGER KNUCKLE AXLES, across the width of the palm. Do NOT rotate the hinge mount sideways and do not restore the old circular forward-facing screw. All joints fold in the SAME front-to-back plane as the fingers, but the thumb acts as the opposite jaw.

Repose the two thumb links in DEPTH:
- The proximal thumb link projects forward OUT of the palm toward the camera, at roughly a right angle to the palm. Its broad side surface is visible.
- The distal thumb link bends back toward the palm and finger row, so its contact pad faces INWARD / AWAY FROM THE CAMERA toward the four finger contact pads. The thumb tip points toward the index/middle knuckles from a position in FRONT of the palm, not upward alongside the index finger.
- This makes an unmistakable bent opposing hook / C-shaped pincer in side profile, with a visible open grasping space between thumb pad and palm/fingers. It remains a blunt mechanical digit, not a sharp claw.
- Show it lower than the finger knuckles and offset just enough toward the thumb side to avoid concealing any finger. A small amount of overlap over the lower side of the palm is appropriate to show that the thumb stands forward in depth. It must be physically attached, never floating.
- The pad on the thumb tip faces the finger pads, like the two opposing jaws of a clamp. It does NOT face the viewer like the finger pads.

Keep the thumb links simple and faceted, with the SAME dark hinge-barrel construction as the other fingers. Use only the existing two links and existing root, no extra articulation, ball joint, sideways swivel, decorative parts or extra digit. Exactly five digits. Do not change anything else.

items.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: corrected single-view reference image for a low-poly mech hand to be modeled through Tripo.

INPUT ROLES:
Image 1 is the hand image to edit. Its FOUR LONG FINGERS ARE APPROVED: preserve their shapes, three-link construction, relative lengths, spacing, hinges, low-poly style and pose exactly.
Image 2 is the owner's AC6 hand reference. Use it to understand the OPPOSING THUMB, substantial palm and mechanical wrist connection. Do not reproduce Blender UI or the full arm.

Make these THREE specific corrections to Image 1:

1. MOST IMPORTANT: REBUILD THE THUMB AS AN OPPOSED JAW WITH HINGE AXES PARALLEL TO THE FOUR FINGER HINGES. The old thumb is wrong: it fans sideways in the palm plane around a pin pointing out of the palm. Remove that side-splaying thumb mount completely. All thumb hinge pins must instead run ACROSS THE WIDTH OF THE PALM, in exactly the same direction as the finger knuckle axles. The thumb can fold only in the same front-to-back bending direction as the fingers, closing AGAINST them from the opposite side of a grip.
Place the thumb root lower on the palm on the thumb side, raised forward off the palm surface on a fixed angular bridge. Show a short two-link mechanical thumb extending toward the finger row, parallel to the fingers' length in front projection, but standing forward of the palm in depth as an opposing jaw. Partly bend it inward so its contact pad visibly faces the four fingers' contact pads. Its visible hinges should look like smaller versions of the FOUR FINGER HINGES, with matching parallel barrels. It must not fan diagonally out to the left like a human thumb. No large circular bolt face looking straight at the camera on its base. No perpendicular pivot, side-swing, swivel, ball joint, multidirectional thumb mound, claw or extra digit. The thumb should be individually visible beside the index finger, with a clear depth gap from the palm. Exactly four long fingers plus ONE thumb.

2. PALM: make the palm visibly larger relative to the unchanged fingers: extend its length from knuckles toward wrist by about 35 percent and widen it modestly by about 10 percent. Give it substantial angular mechanical construction, closer to the AC6 reference: a broad central palm plate, a recessed dark structural border, and two simple stepped side armor cheeks. A few purposeful large planes and shallow recesses, not a blank slab. Retain low-poly shapes, restrained single-edge chamfers, no tiny screws, decorative greebles or elaborate surface paneling.

3. WRIST: completely replace the long skinny plug and toy-like collar. Use a SHORT, BROAD, LOAD-BEARING MECHANICAL WRIST COUPLING, roughly two-thirds of the new palm width. It is a substantial faceted drum captured by a blocky U-shaped support at the heel of the palm, with one broad stepped flange and a short thick terminal mounting stub. Show clear mechanical separation between palm and coupling and a readable attachment face at the end. Make it look like a structural robot wrist joint, with depth and purposeful interlocking forms, not a thin straight Lego peg. No long shaft, stacked thin rings, screw threads or full forearm.

PRESERVE: the exact four long fingers from image 1, gray palette, matte material, soft neutral studio lighting, white background and clean single-object presentation. Keep the same palm-facing mild three-quarter camera; show a little more depth only if essential to make the opposing thumb unambiguous. Reframe or zoom out enough to contain the larger palm and coupling, with white margin around all fingertips and the wrist. ONE hand, ONE view, all five digits readable, no text, arrows, inset diagrams, second hand, weapon or stand.

items.title: v001 - Owner rejected; fingers retained
items.alt: One isolated gray low-poly mechanical hand with four separate segmented fingers, a shorter thumb in a single-axis hinge bracket, and a projecting faceted wrist attachment on a white background
items.body:
**Owner rejected on 5 November 2026.** The thumb is not correctly opposing or aligned with the other finger axes. The attachment is too thin and simple, resembling a Lego piece. The palm is too small relative to the fingers and too basic. The four long fingers are accepted and should be retained.

The earlier agent review below did not establish the required opposing-thumb geometry and is superseded by this feedback.

Generated from the palm and back close-ups of the supplied rounded AC6 mech hand using the built-in image generator. This is a single view of one hand, with all five digits and the wrist connector visible.

The opposing thumb uses a straight axle between rigid bracket ears. Its further links also read as simple hinges, with no ball, swivel turret or organic thumb mound. The palm is plain, the finger links are faceted, and the wrist ends in an exposed shaft and collar.

Agent visual review passed for digit count, full framing, simplified geometry and visible hinge construction. Owner acceptance is pending. The image establishes appearance; the generated mesh will still need its joints and topology checked.

items.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: a single clear image-to-3D reference of a reusable low-poly mech hand, for the owner to use in Tripo.

Input image 1: palm-side geometry reference from the owner's AC6 model. Input image 2: back-side reference of the SAME hand. Transform and simplify this hand, isolate it from the rest of the mech, and re-present it as ONE clean modeling reference. Do not reproduce the Blender UI, forearm armor, background or multiple views.

Subject: ONE complete mechanical hand, four slim separate fingers in a row plus ONE shorter opposing side thumb, exactly FIVE digits. Preserve the references' compact rectangular palm, nearly equal-length finger arrangement, industrial proportions and narrow wrist transition. Three simple angular links per long finger. Fingers extended in a relaxed almost-straight pose with small clear gaps so every digit and joint is visible.

CRITICAL THUMB MECHANISM: the thumb must look constrained to simple one-axis hinge bending, like the references. Its root sits between two rigid parallel bracket ears and turns on ONE visible straight axle, like a door hinge or plier jaw. The thumb closes toward the fingers in one fixed plane. Keep the root mount compact and angular. Any further thumb-link hinges use parallel pin axes in that same bending plane. Show the pin end and enclosing bracket clearly. NO ball-and-socket joint, spherical knuckle, swivel turret, universal joint, rotating thumb pad, organic human thumb mound or multidirectional thumb base. The thumb is open enough that the entire root hinge is unobscured; it does not cross or hide the index finger.

Wrist attachment: at the base of the palm show a distinct short narrow straight octagonal mechanical connector shaft, a single simple collar and a flat terminal mating face. It must visibly project beyond the palm so another forearm can attach to it. The connector is attached to the hand, not floating or exploded. No forearm or cuff beyond this connector; no deep socket hole.

Geometry: visibly LOW POLY and MUCH simpler than the reference. Broad flat faces, rectangular finger links with one small chamfer on silhouette corners, shallow plain palm armor, simple six- or eight-sided hinge barrels. Remove all decorative layered plates, bolts, engraved outlines, inset panels, vents, tiny fasteners and internal machinery. Preserve articulated construction and slim proportions, not a mitten or bulky toy hand. Simple medium-light gray solid surfaces and darker gray joints, neutral matte material, no weathering or mirror gloss.

Camera and presentation: one isolated hand, fingers pointing upward and wrist connector downward. Near-orthographic three-quarter view from the palm and thumb side, only a slight 20-degree turn so all four fingers are individually visible and the thumb hinge and palm thickness are easy to read. Entire hand and terminal connector fully in frame with comfortable margins. Plain white background, even soft studio illumination, minimal ambient shadow. Sharp clean edges and good separation between fingers and background. One object, one view, no labels, text, arrows, diagrams, insets, wireframe, pedestal, weapons or extra components. This is a practical shape reference, not a dramatic hero illustration.

items.title: Preferred wrist connection: rounded mech on the right
items.alt: Palm side of the rounded mech hand, showing an exposed layered wrist collar and a narrow link between the forearm and palm
items.body:
The exposed collar and narrower link create a readable sequence: **forearm armor → wrist joint → palm**. The palm has a substantial center and four closely spaced fingers, with the thumb offset to one side near the wrist. The fingers have three articulated sections and nearly equal overall lengths.

Keep this separation in the shared design. The forearm shell may vary between mechs; the connector, palm, finger proportions and articulation should remain consistent. The layered ring details can become one simple faceted collar.

Source: owner-supplied live Blender scene, rounded mech, anatomical left arm mesh `mesh[0]`, armature `Master`. Other objects were temporarily hidden for this capture; no geometry was removed.

items.title: Back and outer wrist: keep the silhouette, reduce detail
items.alt: Back of the rounded mech hand with broad palm armor, four segmented fingers, an offset thumb and forearm armor around the wrist
items.body:
The back reads as one broad armor mass over the mechanism. The forearm tapers toward the wrist, with armor extending around part of the joint. Circular details, stepped plates and small recesses add density without defining the main hand shape.

Proposed simplification: one shallow faceted palm shell, one angular thumb-root block, simple finger segments with narrow joint gaps, and a clearly exposed wrist collar. Preserve useful silhouette bevels; omit modeled bolts, inset borders, repeated thin plates and internal mechanisms hidden during normal play.

items.title: Comparison: blocky mech on the left
items.alt: Palm side of the blocky mech hand at the same inspection angle, with its palm sitting close to the large forearm armor
items.body:
This hand uses the same broad arrangement of four straight fingers plus an offset thumb. Its palm sits much closer to the forearm shell, making the connection less distinct. The simpler surface treatment is useful, but the shared hand should retain the more visible wrist separation of the rounded reference.

Source: anatomical left arm mesh `mesh[0].001`, armature `Master.001`. These captures show an extended hand. Equipped weapons were visible in the initial scene, but a closed grip and contact clearance were not verified.

items.title: Earlier construction proposal - mesh checks after Tripo
items.body:
**Route update:** use the new image to generate the first mesh with Tripo. The following construction notes are earlier modeling proposals, not an instruction to manually build a mesh now. Thumb hinges must share a fixed bending plane, with no multi-axis base.

Build one editable hand and mirror it for the opposite side. Keep four individually articulated fingers plus one opposing thumb. Use three simple sections per finger so a weapon grip can wrap around a handle; keep the index independently controllable.

Start with the rounded reference's compact, relatively thin palm. Its dominant-weight palm region measures approximately **length 1.19 × width 1.00 × thickness 0.61**. This is a bounding-box ratio including attached details, not an exact palm shell specification. The blocky reference is similar in length but thicker (about 0.76 relative to width).

For the first blockout, try an exposed wrist link about **half to two-thirds of the palm width**, with visible separation roughly **one-quarter of the palm width** between the palm body and the end of the forearm shell. These are proposed design proportions, not measurements or approved dimensions. Use a six- or eight-sided collar and a simple hinge shape instead of layered rings. Keep the fingers slim and close together, with readable gaps and an offset thumb capable of closing toward them.

Define a common wrist attachment point and orientation on the hand. Give each forearm its own adapter to this interface. Check open, relaxed and weapon-grip poses before fixing the connector dimensions. A held-weapon socket belongs on the hand; its offset must be established against the game's actual handle geometry. Absolute scale and the final skeleton remain open.

items.title: Triangle budget: starting proposal
items.body:
The inspected hand regions contain **1,820 triangles** on the blocky reference and **4,106 triangles** on the rounded reference. These counts include the palm and fingers, excluding the forearm; wrist geometry is not separately classified in the source. Counting uses triangles whose vertices all have their strongest weight in the hand or finger groups. There are no boundary triangles crossing that region in these two meshes. Imported vertex counts are higher because vertices can be split at seams, so triangles are the useful comparison here.

Proposed target: **700–1,000 triangles per hand including the new wrist connector**, or 1,400–2,000 for a pair. This is a planning range, not an approved budget or a measured finished mesh. Prioritize the wrist outline, finger articulation and thumb clearance. Use small single-step bevels only where they improve silhouette or highlights.

[Download inspection measurements](assets/shared-hand/reference-study-v001/inspection.json). Verify the final triangulated count after modeling, then judge the result at the actual Unity gameplay camera distance.

items.title: Next step: owner review, then Tripo
items.body:
Review v003 beside the native thumb-side and side-profile captures. Confirm the thumb mounting and open pose before using the image in Tripo. The current route is reference image first, initial mesh through Tripo, then topology and articulation inspection.

The earlier frontal attempts are rejected history. Do not use their thumb geometry as a modeling reference. No generated image has owner approval yet. No Unity files were changed.
